I'm 61 years old and I've only been farming for two years. Before that I worked construction in the city for decades. My father farmed this land but I didn't pay much attention back then — I was always trying to get out to the city. Now I'm back, and I'm learning as I go. I have 7.7 mu, about the same as my neighbor Lao Zhang across the road. There are three of us in the house — me, my wife, and our son — but my son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang and only comes back for harvest, so for most of the year it's just me and my wife doing the farm work.

Last year was my second year with wheat. I planted the whole 7.7 mu and got about 360 jin per mu. Not great, but Lao Zhang got 400 jin, so I think if I follow what he does more closely I can do better. I'm still figuring things out.

**For wheat this year:** I'm going to plant around October 10th, same as everyone in the village. You can't plant too early or the wheat grows too tall before winter and freezes. I'll buy improved wheat seed from the seed shop — about 15 jin per mu, that's roughly 7 or 8 kg. Last year I used less and the stand was a bit thin. I plow the field first with my small hand tractor, then spread fertilizer and plant.

For fertilizer, Lao Zhang uses one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that's 50 jin, about 25 kg. I did the same last year. Then in spring at jointing time, he puts another half bag of urea, about 25 jin. I only did 15 jin last year because I was short on cash after buying the maize seed, but this year I'll try to do the full half bag like him. The extension fellow came to the village once and said something about soil tests, but I don't really understand that. I just know Lao Zhang's wheat always looks greener and thicker than mine.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter so the seedlings don't dry out, once at jointing in March or April when it starts growing fast, and once when the grain is filling in May. Each time costs about 20 yuan for electricity to pump from the well. It's expensive but you have to do it — last year I skipped the winter irrigation and I think that's partly why my yield was lower.

For weeds, I spray herbicide once after planting. Last year I didn't and the chenopodium weeds were terrible. If I see aphids or other bugs in spring I might spray insecticide, but only if I really see them — chemicals cost money and I'm not going to spray just in case.

**For maize:** I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. The window is very tight — sometimes only five or six days between harvest and planting. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, then we immediately plant maize. I buy hybrid maize seed — about 5 jin per mu. It's expensive, about 50 yuan per mu, but everyone says you can't save your own maize seed, the yield drops too much.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the holes at planting time, about one bag per mu same as wheat. Some people topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high, but last year I didn't because I was tired and the money was tight after all the wheat costs, and the yield was still okay. Maybe I'll do it this year if I have time and cash left — Lao Zhang says it helps.

Maize irrigation depends on the summer rain. If it rains well in July and August, maybe once. If it's dry like two years ago, twice. Pumping costs money so I watch the sky and talk to Lao Zhang about whether he's irrigating.

Labor is mostly me and my wife. For wheat harvest we definitely hire the combine — you can't cut wheat by hand anymore, there's no time. For maize harvest we might do it by hand or hire a small machine, depending on whether my son can get leave from the factory to help. Last year he came home for three days and we did it mostly ourselves.

I'm worried about money. I only have about 3,000 yuan saved for inputs this year. Fertilizer prices keep going up. If I have to choose, I'd rather cut back on maize topdressing than on wheat fertilizer, because wheat is the main crop and I understand it a little better. Also, if I apply too little fertilizer and the yield crashes, that's worse than wasting a little too much — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps, that's what my father used to say. I just hope the weather is normal and I can get through another year without making too many mistakes.
